description: Experience the ultimate comfort food with our classic Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani. This beloved dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce, subtly spiced and finished with a swirl of butter and cream. It's a truly indulgent and satisfying meal that captures the essence of authentic Indian cuisine.

ingredients.item: Boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 mins

ingredients.item: Canned crushed tomatoes or tomato puree

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the cubed chicken with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook in batches, if necessary, until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside, leaving any drippings in the pan.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and saute until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the soaked cashews and crushed tomatoes.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1 tablespoon coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and 1 teaspoon kasoori methi (crushed) to the pan. Add sugar and salt to taste. Pour in 1/2 cup water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. Carefully transfer the sauce to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to do this in batches. Strain the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth consistency, discarding any solids.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan and bring it to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir well to coat the chicken. Continue to simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce and heat through completely.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream and a final pat of butter (about 1 tablespoon) until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the marinated chicken slightly on a grill or in a very hot pan before adding to the sauce.
Always strain the sauce after blending for the silkiest, restaurant-quality texture. This step makes a significant difference.
Adjust the level of spice by varying the amount of red chili powder and green chilies. For a milder version, reduce or omit the chilies entirely.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a global culinary phenomenon that has captured the hearts and palates of millions. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, this iconic Indian chicken recipe stands out with its incredibly rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based gravy. It’s the ultimate comfort food, a harmonious blend of tender chicken, aromatic spices, and a luxurious texture that makes it a perennial favorite in Indian restaurants worldwide and a must-try for any home cook looking to explore the vibrant flavors of India.

The allure of Indian cuisine lies in its complexity and depth of flavor, achieved through a masterful use of spices and cooking techniques. Among the myriad of dishes, Butter Chicken holds a special place, often being the first introduction for many to the wonders of Indian food. Its mild spice profile, balanced with a delightful sweetness and tang, makes it approachable yet undeniably exotic. Whether you’re a seasoned chef or a kitchen novice, mastering this classic dish is a rewarding experience that promises to bring a touch of Indian culinary magic to your dining table.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its story began in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, where Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder, reputedly invented the dish. The tale goes that leftover tandoori chicken pieces were simmered in a rich tomato and butter-based gravy to prevent them from drying out, creating an instant classic. This innovative approach transformed simple leftovers into a globally celebrated delicacy.

At its core, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoor-cooked, but pan-fried or baked works perfectly for home cooking) bathed in a velvety smooth sauce. The distinct flavor profile comes from a blend of tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and a carefully selected array of Indian spices such as garam masala, fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), and red chili powder. What truly sets it apart is the generous use of butter and cream, which impart an unparalleled richness and a signature silken texture to the gravy. While often compared to Chicken Tikka Masala, Butter Chicken is typically milder, sweeter, and focuses more on the creamy tomato base, whereas Tikka Masala often has a more pronounced spice and tang.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components. Don't be intimidated by the list; most ingredients are readily available and contribute significantly to the final masterpiece.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (or more, for richness!)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 fresh large tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in hot water for 15 minutes, optional but recommended for creaminess)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon sugar (to balance acidity)
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
*   Salt to taste

For Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home:

Step 1: Marinate the Chicken. In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat all the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for maximum flavor and tenderness.

Step 2: Cook the Chicken. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base. In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Step 4: Build the Gravy Flavors. Add the crushed tomatoes (or pureed fresh tomatoes), soaked cashews (if using), red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric powder, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are well-cooked and the oil starts to separate.

Step 5: Blend the Gravy. Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silken texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for achieving that signature restaurant-style smoothness.

Step 6: Finish the Gravy. Return the smooth gravy to the pan over low heat. Stir in the sugar and kasoori methi. Add the heavy cream and gently simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the gravy thickens slightly and is heated through. Do not boil the gravy vigorously after adding cream.

Step 7: Combine and Serve. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir to coat the chicken evenly and let it gently simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect, rich, and flavorful Butter Chicken is easier with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor, making your chicken incredibly succulent.
*   **The Smoothest Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is non-negotiable for an authentic texture. Straining it afterwards takes it to another level of luxury.
*   **Kasoori Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are essential. Lightly toast them in a dry pan for a minute before crushing them between your palms and adding to the gravy. This releases their unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor that defines Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance is Everything:** The sugar in the recipe isn't just for sweetness; it balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and adjust to achieve a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and savory.
*   **Don't Boil the Cream:** Once you add the cream, keep the heat low and just simmer. Boiling cream at high heat can cause it to curdle, ruining the gravy's smooth consistency.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality butter and ripe, flavorful tomatoes (canned San Marzano tomatoes are excellent if fresh aren't in season).

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with various accompaniments. The classic way to enjoy this rich curry is with:

*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed or jeera (cumin) rice perfectly soaks up the creamy gravy.
*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is ideal for scooping up every last drop of the delicious sauce.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads also make excellent choices.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip with cucumber or mint can provide a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic recipe is divine, you can easily adapt Butter Chicken to suit different preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Vegetarian Option:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or even chickpeas for a delightful Paneer Makhani or Tofu Makhani.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a slit green chili during the gravy simmering stage.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some heavy cream with light cream or even a dairy-free alternative like cashew cream for a lighter version.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have nut allergies, you can omit the cashews. The gravy will still be creamy, though slightly less rich. You can also use a thickener like a cornstarch slurry at the end.

This timeless Butter Chicken recipe is a testament to the magic of Indian cooking. With its tender chicken and luscious, buttery gravy, it promises a truly satisfying meal that will transport your taste buds straight to India. Don't hesitate to embark on this culinary adventure; the reward is a dish that's rich in flavor, history, and comfort. Enjoy creating and savoring this magnificent Indian classic!
